issues.issue: Is toxic psychosis from self-induced intoxication a 'mental disorder' under s.16 Cr. C. exempting criminal responsibility?
issues.applicant_position: Toxic psychosis from intoxication is a mental disorder affecting vulnerable individuals, thus qualifying under s.16 defence.
issues.respondent_position: Toxic psychosis from self-induced intoxication is excluded as a mental disorder under s.16 per Cooper and case law.
issues.result_text: Appellant's toxic psychosis was self-induced intoxication, not a legal mental disorder under s.16 Cr. C.

issues.issue: Does s.33.1 Cr. C. limit the scope of the defence of not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder in s.16 Cr. C.?
issues.applicant_position: Appellant argues s.33.1 wrongly limits s.16 defence and courts confused the defences.
issues.respondent_position: s.33.1 Cr. C. excludes self-induced intoxication defence for violent offences but does not limit s.16 defence scope.
issues.result_text: Court clarifies s.16 and s.33.1 defences are mutually exclusive but does not limit s.16 scope here.

issues.issue: Did the Court of Appeal err in applying s.33.1 Cr. C. instead of s.16 Cr. C. to appellant's toxic psychosis?
issues.applicant_position: Appellant contends Court of Appeal wrongly applied s.33.1 and should have applied s.16 defence.
issues.respondent_position: Court of Appeal correctly applied s.33.1 Cr. C. as toxic psychosis was self-induced intoxication, not mental disorder.
issues.result_text: Court finds Court of Appeal correctly applied s.33.1 Cr. C. and dismisses appeal.
